Name: River Ahava
Description: A river or canal in Babylonia where Ezra gathered the returning exiles on their way back to Jerusalem. There Ezra proclaimed a fast, that the company might humble themselves before God and seek a safe journey for themselves, their children, and their goods. The exact canal is unidentified, and this entry does not guess at its course or modern course.
BiblicalSignificance: Ahava is where the return from exile paused for prayer before it moved. Ezra would not ask the king for soldiers and horsemen; instead the exiles fasted and sought God's protection for the road, and God answered. The gathering at Ahava also exposed a practical problem for the journey: no Levites were found among those assembled, and Ezra sent for ministers for the house of God before setting out.
